question: What follows if knowability belongs to all knowers at once?
premises: under all-knower knowability, knowing is held in common
then no single knower owns knowability
so knowability cannot be any entity's private property
inference: Private and public horns both kill perceptibility-as-property.
uncertainties: dilemma stated baldly; resolution comes after v28
plain_english: Under all-knower knowability there is no single-knower knowability — therefore perceptibility so-called is no entity's property at all.
